title: acme-pipeline: moving the old cron estate onto the platform
subtitle: Which of the 17 cron jobs in legacy/ to keep, rebuild or retire, and how to move them in waves that can be checked and rolled back.

verdict.text: The move is smaller than 17 jobs suggests: 10 retire (six dead, two already done by platform jobs, one copy, one folded into its partner), one moves as it is and six are rebuilt, in six waves. Before the orders chain can move, two things must be settled: the logistics partner's 05:30 feed has to keep reading the ERP directly at 01:00, because the platform's ERP file arrives at 05:38–07:37, and the platform needs a cost source for the month-end margin. The owners also have to confirm the dead jobs and name who reads the `dw.*` outputs.

sections.title: Findings
sections.intro: Each finding was checked in the scripts, not just taken from the inventory script's output. Times are from the inventory export of 2026-11-04 06:00.

items.title: The partner feed cannot be built on the platform's ERP orders file: it arrives too late
items.evidence: The partner "plans the next day's deliveries" from the file sent at 05:30. In the last 31 deliveries the platform's `sources/erp/<date>/orders.csv` arrived between 05:38 and 07:37, and on working days between 07:06 and 07:37. None arrived before 05:30. Today's feed instead reads `erp.order_lines` straight from the ERP database at 01:00 (`nightly_orders_extract.sh:4`). [high]
items.fix: Rebuild the extract and the send as one platform job that still reads the ERP (through `ERP_DSN`, or `erp_replica` if it carries order lines) at 01:00. Do not feed the partner from `load_erp_orders`.

items.title: If the 01:00 extract fails, the partner gets yesterday's orders under today's name
items.evidence: `DAY` comes from the clock, and `put` uploads whatever `/data/extracts/orders_latest.csv` holds. Cron runs at 05:30 whether or not the 01:00 extract ran, because the inventory's `depends_on` is not enforced by cron. A failed extract leaves the previous day's file, which goes out as `acme_orders_<today>.csv`. [med] The host's logs would show whether this has happened.

items.title: Two jobs write `dw.stock_snapshot` at the same minute, and which one ends last decides the result
items.evidence: Both run at `0 3 * * *`. The load truncates the table and inserts today's stock. The fix sets negative `on_hand` to 0 where `snapshot_date = current_date`. If the fix runs before the insert commits, it updates 0 rows and the store report gets negative stock, which the fix exists to prevent. [high] that the race exists; [med] that it is lost on some nights, since psql commits each statement unless run with `-1`.
items.fix: Rebuild as one step that writes `greatest(on_hand, 0)`, or that flags the negative rows if the report owner prefers. Retire `fix_stock_snapshot`.

items.title: The price list loader reads the staging file through a link the inventory does not declare, and loads yesterday's prices if staging fails
items.evidence: `stage_price_list` writes `/data/staging/price_list.csv` at 02:00. `load_price_list` reads it at 02:20, but its `depends_on` is empty. If the copy from `/mnt/purchasing` fails, `set -eu` stops the stage step but leaves the old staged file, and the load truncates `dw.price_list` and reloads the old prices without any error. A slow copy could also leave a half-written file. The two jobs have different owners (m.lukic, d.vujic).
items.fix: Rebuild as one platform job: copy, convert CP1250 to UTF-8, check the file date and row count, then load. The job must fail rather than load a stale file.

items.title: The month-end margin needs `cost_amount`, which the platform's orders data does not have
items.evidence: The margin is `sum(amount) - sum(cost_amount)` from `dw.orders`. Neither `silver.orders` nor the ERP orders file has a cost column. Until a cost source exists on the platform, `dw.orders`, and with it `load_dw_orders` and the legacy extract, cannot be retired. [high]
items.fix: Agree a cost source with the ERP team, either a contract change to add cost to `orders.csv` or a replica table, before wave 6.

items.title: Six jobs are dead: still in the crontab, but with no successful run for 216 to 345 days
items.evidence: `old_loyalty_points`: last run 2026-02-28, 249 runs missed. `store_kpi_v1`: 2026-04-02, 215 missed. `promo_export_2025`: 2026-03-30, 31 missed. `supplier_scorecard`: 2025-11-24, 49 missed. `fax_order_import`: 2025-12-19, 4,086 missed. `cleanup_tmp_tables`: 2026-01-11, 42 missed. Two of them read inputs no job writes (`dw.orders_v1`, `dw.supplier_deliveries`). Because the lines are still in the crontab, these jobs probably start and fail on every schedule [med].
items.fix: Retire each one after its owner confirms. Keep the script and a snapshot of its last output.

items.title: The fax import may have stopped while orders kept arriving
items.evidence: The job loads files the fax-to-mail gateway saves in `/data/fax_inbox/` and moves them to `done/`. If the gateway still saves files, every fax order since 2025-12-19 is still in the inbox and was never loaded into `dw.fax_orders`. [guess] The folder was not inspected.
items.fix: Before retiring, count the `*.csv` files in `/data/fax_inbox/` that have not been moved to `done/`.

items.title: The two sales exports are the same query, written to two files
items.evidence: The scripts are byte-identical (sha256 `1d719033a25a`). Both say "for finance" and write the last 7 days per store and day, one to `/data/exports/store_sales.csv` (d.vujic, 05:00) and one to `/data/exports/finance/sales_by_store.csv` (t.krsmanovic, 05:15). Finance already reads `gold.sales_daily` every day for the cash plan (31 of 31 days in `ops/query_log.csv`).
items.fix: Keep one export, built from `gold.sales_daily.gross_revenue`, only if someone still picks the file up. Point the readers of the other file at it.

items.title: `daily_customer_sync` duplicates the platform's `rebuild_customers` and keeps a second copy of personal data
items.evidence: Both jobs reload the ERP customer master in full. `dw.customers` holds `tax_id`, `email` and `phone`. `silver.customers` leaves out quarantined rows: 3 customers a day without a tax id since 2026-10-20. It is also ready at 04:15 instead of 00:45.
items.fix: Retire the legacy job once the readers of `dw.customers` accept the 04:15 time and the 3 quarantined rows.

items.title: Nobody knows who reads most of the old outputs
items.evidence: No job reads 13 of the outputs, including `dw.customers`, `dw.price_list`, `dw.stock_snapshot`, `dw.margin_monthly` and both export files. The query log only covers platform tables, so the readers of the old warehouse are not on record anywhere in the repo.
items.fix: Get a week of query log from the old warehouse, and the file-access or pickup log for `/data/exports`, before waves 2 to 4.

items.title: The SFTP password is passed on the command line
items.evidence: `lftp -u "acme_export,${SFTP_PASSWORD}"`: the value comes from the host environment, so there is no literal in the script. While the job runs, though, the password shows in the host's process list.
items.fix: Put the password in the platform's secret store, use key-based login if the partner supports it, and rotate the password at cutover.

items.title: `cleanup_tmp_tables` drops every `dw.tmp_*` table, not only those older than a week
items.evidence: The comment says "older than a week", but the loop drops every match without checking age. It is retired anyway, since nothing on the platform writes `dw.tmp_*`.

items.title: The crontab lines themselves are not in the repo
items.evidence: The exports are written "by the cron line", so the CSV delimiter, header and encoding cannot be read from the repo, and neither can the job's MAILTO or log target. The README also says some owners have left, without saying which.

sections.title: Links between jobs
sections.intro: Built from what each script reads and writes, not from `depends_on`. The price list link is the only one the inventory does not declare. The cron line enforces none of them: each job simply starts at its own time.

sections.title: Waves
sections.intro: Each wave keeps the old cron line and the old target untouched until it is signed off. A rebuilt reader that no longer reads an old table (for example an export built from `gold.sales_daily`) can move before that table's old writer. The orders chain is split so that the old extract keeps feeding `load_dw_orders` until wave 6.

items.title: Wave 1: retire the six dead jobs (runs alongside the others)
items.text: `old_loyalty_points`, `store_kpi_v1`, `promo_export_2025`, `supplier_scorecard`, `fax_order_import`, `cleanup_tmp_tables`. Each one only after its owner (or the team lead, where the owner has left) says yes. First count the waiting files in `/data/fax_inbox/`. Archive each script and take a row count and snapshot of its last output. Comment out the cron line, but do not delete it or drop the tables.

items.title: Wave 2: customers
items.text: Point the readers of `dw.customers` at `silver.customers`, which the platform already rebuilds daily at 04:15. Parallel run for 14 days, then disable `daily_customer_sync`. Readers must accept the 04:15 time and the quarantined rows. This is the smallest internal group and makes a good first move.

items.title: Wave 3: price list and stock snapshot (two independent groups)
items.text: Price list: one platform job that copies from the purchasing share, converts CP1250 to UTF-8, checks the file and loads, replacing `stage_price_list` and `load_price_list`. The platform needs read access to `/mnt/purchasing` first. Stock: one step that writes the 03:00 snapshot with the negative-stock rule applied, replacing `load_stock_snapshot` and `fix_stock_snapshot`. If the store report's owner agrees, point the report at `gold.stock_levels` instead and build nothing. Parallel run 14 days each.

items.title: Wave 4: sales exports
items.text: One export from `gold.sales_daily` (gross revenue for the last 7 days per store and day) replaces both files, but only if finance still picks a file up. Otherwise both retire, because finance already reads the table. `gold.sales_daily` is ready by 08:00, not 05:00, so finance must accept the later time. Parallel run 14 days.

items.title: Wave 5: partner feed
items.text: A platform job extracts yesterday's order lines from the ERP at 01:00, checks the order date and row count, and sends to the partner at 05:30, replacing `send_partner_orders`. The password moves to the secret store. During the parallel run (21 days) the new file goes to a test folder the partner provides. Cut over on a date agreed with the partner, mid-week. The old `nightly_orders_extract` stays on, because `load_dw_orders` still reads its file.

items.title: Wave 6: month-end margin and the end of `dw.orders`
items.text: Needs the agreed cost source first. Rebuild `month_end_margin` on `silver.orders` plus cost, with a parallel run that covers one real 15th: 2026-12-15 if the cost source lands by early December, otherwise 2027-01-15. After sign-off, retire `load_dw_orders` and the old `nightly_orders_extract`.

sections.title: Acceptance and rollback
sections.intro: The numbers are agreed before each parallel run starts. During the run both versions run, the new output goes nowhere outside, and the numbers are compared daily. Rollback always means re-enabling the old cron line and pointing the readers back. The old target is not touched until sign-off.
